title: The Free Table
logline: On a dry-zone road with no restaurant in sight, a family that has fed passing strangers for free every day for years hands Chathura a plate before he even asks, and keeps insisting it was nothing.

object.note: Object 6 (identity not chosen) could enter only if something is genuinely given freely to Chathura along with the meal. Never staged.

thread_in.thread: In that gap, goodness can be chosen: from a festival stall's free food to a roadside family that has fed passing strangers for years and hands Chathura a plate before he asks.

thread_out.thread: Giving without keeping count becomes weighing honestly when no one checks: a market vendor whose old scales nobody doubts.

requirements: A genuine roadside stall or household that feeds passing strangers without payment as an ongoing practice
Willingness to be filmed over enough time to show the pattern, not a single staged act
Real traffic and real strangers, not arranged visitors

lesson.in_simple_terms: Everyday giving, like handing a stranger a plate of food, is the kind of goodness the texts call 'great', not because it is rare or lofty but because it is everywhere. It counts whether it is done with a big smile or as a quiet daily habit.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: නාඳුනන කෙනෙකුට බත් පිඟානක් දීම වැනි එදිනෙදා දීම, දුර්ලභ නිසා නොව හැම තැනම බොහෝ දෙනා කරන නිසා 'මහා කුසල' ලෙස හැඳින්වෙන අතර, එය සතුටින් කළත් පුරුද්දෙන් නිහඬව කළත් යහපතක්මයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma describes the wholesome mind of ordinary life, the one that arises when people give, keep precepts or help, as coming in eight kinds: joyful or even-toned, with or without understanding of action and its results, and spontaneous or prompted. One source explains that this goodness is called 'great' because it is common to many people everywhere, not because it is higher than other kinds. The texts also teach that a mind never arises alone: it always comes with a group of mental factors that arise and cease with it, and only those needed for that moment's work arise.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The plate arrives before Chathura asks, a stranger who tries to pay is waved off, and the family's practised motions happen with no cash register and no record of who paid. At the end of the day the family eats what is left over, and their insistence that it was nothing lets the viewer see how ordinary, and how complete, this kind of goodness is.

key_terms.en: 'great' wholesome: everyday goodness, called great because it is common to many
accompanied by joy / by neutral, even feeling
mental factor; a quality that arises with and depends on a mind

lesson.caution: This does not mean kindness only counts when it feels joyful; the texts treat calm, even-toned giving as fully wholesome, with joy depending on conditions.
lesson.builds_on: The previous stage found a gap inside each moment of perception where action is chosen; this film shows what fills that gap when goodness is chosen, in the plainest form of giving.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
